description: Our team is built on understanding, open communication, and collaboration. Our goal is to successfully tackle the challenge we choose for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, while learning, sharing knowledge, having fun, and making the most of everyone's skills and abilities to achieve our common goal.
summary:
Based on information and resources provided by NASA for this challenge, as well as reference images, I created a museum retracing the history of Martian and lunar rovers and their missions. Even though NASA has left these rovers behind, it has never forgotten them, and neither have we forgotten everything they helped us learn and accomplish, from mapping planets and analyzing rocks to conducting experiments. This shows just how valuable and essential these rovers are to astronomical and space research.
My museum commemorates their achievements by presenting what they looked like, simplified versions of their plans, why they were built, what their missions were, and what they were made of. It is divided into two sections, the Lunar Hall and the Martian Hall, to make everything more organized and easier to understand. Above all, my goal is to make NASA's achievements accessible, clear, and understandable to younger generations, especially people my age.
details: My project is an educational museum showcasing the history, missions, designs, and achievements of lunar and Martian rovers. It is divided into two sections, the Lunar Hall and the Martian Hall, presenting simplified plans, reference images, and accessible explanations. Its goal is to make NASA's achievements and space research easier to understand, especially for younger generations. Its impact is mainly educational, encouraging curiosity about astronomy and space exploration while preserving the legacy of these rovers. I used English, a PC as hardware, PowerPoint as software, AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, and NASA's official resources. The project's creativity comes from transforming complex scientific information into an organized, visual, and accessible museum. My friend and I considered accuracy, simplicity, accessibility, organization, and educational value throughout the project.
